abstract.para: While the system to be protected is up and running, create a file backup and generate a recovery system that contains a system-specific &rear; recovery installer. After you have configured &rear;, create the recovery installation system (including the &rear; recovery installer) plus the file backup.

listitem.para: &rear; is installed on the system you want to back up.

topic.para: Perform this procedure on the original machine:

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Create the recovery system, using the -D option to enable verbose mode and debug mode:

listitem.para: For basic backups with tar, use the rear mkbackup command to create both the file backup and the recovery system:
For third-party backup tools, use the rear mkrescue command to create only the recovery system:

step.para: Both commands perform the following steps:

listitem.para: Analyze the target system and gather information, in particular about the disk layout (partitioning, file systems, mount points, etc.) and about the boot loader.

Create a bootable recovery system with the information gathered in the first step. The resulting &rear; recovery installer is specific to this system. It can only be used to re-create this exact system.

step.para: The rear mkbackup command also calls the internal backup tool to back up system files and user files. The rear mkrescue command doesn't create a backup of the files.
If you used rear mkrescue, create a file backup using your third-party backup tool.
Depending on your &rear; configuration, you might need to create a recovery medium by copying the recovery system to a USB . Alternatively, you can use a network boot via PXE.
